title: Decide how the browser reaches the thin-turn API
description:
Resolve docs/MESSAGING.md open question before wiring custom domains.

Options:
1. Same origin — one CloudFront distribution; /api/* behavior proxies to the Lambda function URL (simplest for cookies/CORS; requires unified distribution or web stack owns API alias).
2. api.chattic.us — separate subdomain per environment pointing at the existing thin-turn CloudFront distributions (least invasive; add CORS and env-specific API base URL in Next.js).
3. Keep *.cloudfront.net for API in dev/staging; custom domain only for production web until placement is proven.

Deliverable: decision recorded in docs/MESSAGING.md and docs/DESIGN_CHALLENGES.md; drives the next two tasks.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
**Decision (2026-08-31): same origin.**

Each environment gets one CloudFront distribution on the web hostname (e.g. `chattic.us`, `staging.chattic.us`, `dev.chattic.us`):

- **Default behavior** → S3 origin (Next.js static assets).
- **`/api/*` behavior** → existing thin-turn Lambda function URL origin (caching disabled, same SSE/read-timeout settings as today). A CloudFront Function strips the `/api` prefix before forwarding so FastAPI routes stay at `/channels`, `/turns`, etc.

The browser calls `/api/...` on the same host — no CORS, one ACM cert, one TLS context for SSE.

**Infra consequence:** the per-environment web stack owns the public CloudFront distribution; the thin-turn stack keeps Lambda/SQS/DynamoDB but stops publishing a separate viewer-facing CloudFront (or that distribution becomes an internal origin-only detail). Workers and acceptance scripts may keep using the function URL directly or switch to `https://{site}/api/...`.

Recorded in docs/MESSAGING.md and docs/DESIGN_CHALLENGES.md.
